title: SF434 (2019-2020 Regular): Firearms transfers and private party firearms transfers criminal background checks requirement

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/91/2019/0/SF/434/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced text (as filed; no date given). The bill strikes 'pistol or semiautomatic military-style assault weapon' throughout 624.7131 and 624.7132 and replaces it with 'firearm', and strikes 'yearly' in 624.714 subd. 4. Transfer exclusions (subd. 6 of new section) not quoted. No votes recorded.

operative_text:
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 2): A person who is not a firearms dealer is prohibited from transferring a firearm to any other person who is not a firearms dealer, unless the transferee presents a valid state permit to carry issued under section 624.714 or a valid transferee permit issued under section 624.7131, and a current state or federally issued identification.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 3(d)): Both the transferor and the transferee must retain a copy of the record of transfer and any attachments to the record of transfer for five years following the transfer.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 4(a)): The transferor and transferee of a firearm transferred under this section must produce the record of transfer when a peace officer requests the record as part of a criminal investigation or case.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 7): A transferor or transferee who engages in the transfer of a firearm in violation of this section is guilty of a gross misdemeanor.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7132, subd. 14(a)): No person shall transfer a firearm to another who is not personally known to the transferor unless the proposed transferee presents evidence of identity to the transferor.
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 624.7132, subd. 4): Except as otherwise provided in subdivision 7 or 8, no person shall deliver a firearm to a proposed transferee until five business days after the date the agreement to transfer is delivered to a chief of police or sheriff in accordance with subdivision 1 unless the chief of police or sheriff waives all or a portion of the seven-day waiting period.
Section 4 (Minn. Stat. 624.714, subd. 4(c)): The sheriff must conduct a background check by means of electronic data transfer on a permit holder through the Minnesota Crime Information System and the National Instant Criminal Background Check System at least monthly to ensure continuing eligibility.
